q: How many players from one team are on the court during a basketball game?
note: The very first game, in 1891, was played nine a side because that was how many students turned up.

q: In baseball, how many strikes make a strikeout?
note: A foul ball counts as a strike, but it cannot be the third one unless the batter was bunting.

q: What is the name of Major League Baseball's championship series?
note: The first one was played in 1903 between Boston and Pittsburgh, and Boston won it.

q: In basketball, how many points is a free throw worth?
note: A basket from open play is worth two, or three from behind the arc, a line the NBA only adopted in 1979.

q: How many innings are there in a regulation Major League Baseball game?
note: Baseball has no clock at all, so a tied game simply carries on into extra innings.

q: In ice hockey, what is the name of the hard rubber disc that players shoot at the goal?
note: Pucks are frozen before a game because a warm one bounces awkwardly on the ice.

q: How many players from each team, including the goaltender, are on the ice in ice hockey?
note: Trailing teams often pull the goaltender for an extra attacker in the closing minute, leaving the net empty.

q: How high above the floor is the rim of a basketball hoop?
note: It has not moved since 1891, even though the players have grown a great deal taller since then.

q: In baseball, what is the term for a home run hit while all three bases are occupied?
note: It brings home four runs at once, the most that can be scored on a single swing.

q: In baseball, how many balls does a batter need to be awarded a walk?
note: It is officially recorded as a base on balls, and the batter simply strolls to first.

q: What is the name of the trophy awarded to the champions of the National Hockey League?
note: Every winning player's name is engraved on it, so the trophy carries thousands of names.

q: Which small New York town is home to the Baseball Hall of Fame?
note: It was chosen because of a legend that baseball was invented there, a story historians long ago debunked.

q: During the seventh-inning stretch, baseball crowds traditionally sing which song?
a: Take Me Out to the Ball Game
accept: Take Me Out to the Ballgame
note: It was written in 1908 by two men who, by their own account, had never been to a baseball game.

q: The American college basketball tournament held each spring is popularly known by what name?
note: It is knockout from the first whistle, so a single bad afternoon ends a team's season.

q: Which exhibition basketball team is famous for comic routines performed to the tune Sweet Georgia Brown?
note: Despite the name they were founded in Chicago, and only later borrowed Harlem for its showbusiness ring.

q: Which horse race is run each May at Churchill Downs in Louisville, Kentucky?
note: It is nicknamed the Run for the Roses, and the whole thing is over in about two minutes.

q: Which Canadian-American teacher invented basketball in 1891 using two peach baskets?
note: His first game used a soccer ball, and somebody had to fetch it out of the basket after every score.

q: How many feet apart are the bases on a Major League Baseball diamond?
note: That distance has barely changed since the 1850s and is often called the most perfect number in sport.

q: The winner of which American motor race traditionally drinks a bottle of milk in victory lane?
note: The custom began in 1936 when the winner asked for buttermilk, which he drank at home on hot days.

q: What is the name of the trophy presented to the champions of the National Basketball Association?
note: It is a gold-plated ball dropping into a net, named after a former commissioner of the league.
